title: Snooky's, Morris Levy and Dizzy's house loan
summary: Thomas books Dizzy at Snooky's when Levy won't pay more, then gets Levy to lend six thousand dollars and raise him to fifteen hundred.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Yeah. Dizzy was a good comedian, so... I got involved with that a little bit when Snooky was on 45th Street or 44th Street, and that's how I got close to Dizzy. Because I got him the job down there... Because I was having trouble with Morris Levy. Morris Levy didn't want to pay him more... We was trying to make another fifty dollars. We was only making twelve-hundred dollars; we was trying to get $1250 -- and he just didn't want to pay us no more money. So I went and got him a job for $1500 at Snooky's. And he packed that joint. That's how I got close to Snooky. That's how I was able to bring Ben Webster in town. Because they just gave me the deal to booking the place.

So I went over one night to Birdland, and Morris said, "What's Dizzy doing?" I said, "He's playing over at Snooky's." And it just so happened that the guys at Snooky's was supposed to give us another deal, but they was kind of reneging on the deal. You know, they didn't want... Because, see, Dizzy wanted to buy this house out here in Long Island, and he wanted to get his advance to buy the house. So I told Morris... I actually leveled with him. I

said we were trying to make a deal with Snooky's, because Dizzy wants to borrow some money to buy a house. And he said, "Tell him to call and see me tomorrow. I'll work it out." But see, he told me he'd never book Dizzy no more. But I just never took "no" for an answer. I just had my go at it, and I went to see Joe Davis. I didn't go there to talk no business with Morris, but Morris talked to me and got me in the business... And he just hated... I didn't find it out until later. He hated for an attraction he liked to be playing somewhere else.

So I went over there the next night with Dizzy and told him that Dizzy needed six thousand dollars to make this down-payment on his home out here. So Morris said, "I'll give it to him." He gave him the six thousand dollars, and then raised his price up to fifteen-hundred! Now, we had been trying to get... The only reason I was over at Snooky's was because we couldn't get another fifty dollars from Morris. He gave us the fifteen hundred dollars, and worked out so many weeks for the year, and took the three hundred dollars off to pay for the loan...
Three hundred dollars for what? A week?
Yeah. I think it was three hundred dollars a week. Something like that. Anyway, he got the loan. But he booked him the whole year and gave him a raise of fifteen

hundred dollars a week. And then, the next thing he did, he put him in there... The only time he put Dizzy in there, he put him in there with other stars. He didn't put him in there to draw the weight all by himself. He put him in there with Sarah, all the big stars. And he packed the joint. That's what really got him started out.
